correctness.rationale: The extremal-measure criterion reduces the binary problem to off-zero autocorrelation cancellation. The rectangle witness has Fourier transform 2 or 2 times a unit character value because the distinguished increment has order two. The \(\mathbb Z_7\) signs \((1,-1,-1,-1)\) cancel every nonzero autocorrelation in pairs. For \(\mathbb Z_5\) every nonzero difference has three representations, so a sum of three signs cannot vanish. For the exceptional \(\mathbb Z_4\times\mathbb Z_2\) prototype the order-two difference \((0,1)\) has exactly the two reverse representations, forcing autocorrelation plus or minus 2. These four prototype checks, together with the published exhaustive support classification and invariance under its support operations, prove the iff claim. The bundled finite verifier corroborates but does not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Binary phases are the smallest real unimodular alphabet and correspond to exact perfect periodic autocorrelation. The result gives a complete all-group cardinality-four boundary between Sidon-extreme support geometry and binary flat-spectrum realizability: the rectangle and \(\mathbb Z_7\) geometries admit real signs, whereas the \(\mathbb Z_5\) and exceptional \(\mathbb Z_4\times\mathbb Z_2\) geometries intrinsically require nonbinary phases. This is a structural classification rather than a fixed finite table or a routine parameter increment.
